title: The First Number That Occurs Once

concept.title: Two passes: count, then look again in order
body: A hash map knows **how often** each value occurs, but not **where** the first one is. To find the first value (by position) that occurs exactly once, make two passes: the first pass counts, the second pass goes through the array in its original order and stops at the first element whose count is 1.
Going through the array (not through the map) in the second pass is what gives the "first" element. A map has no reliable order.

statement: Print the first number (reading from left to right) that occurs exactly once in the array. If there is no such number, print `none`.

examples.note: 7 is the first value that occurs once.

hints: First count how often each value occurs.
Then go through the array again in order.
The first element with count 1 is the answer.
